Under the Data Act, the contract may impose a maximum notice period of two months (Article 25(2)(d)). The transition itself must not exceed the mandatory maximum transitional period of 30 calendar days (Article 25(2)(a)); if that is technically unfeasible, the provider must notify the customer within 14 working days, justify this, and may set an alternative transitional period of up to seven months (Article 25(4)), and the customer may also extend the transitional period once (Article 25(5)). As for charges: in March 2026 (before 12 January 2027), the provider may impose only reduced switching charges that do not exceed the costs directly linked to the switching process (Article 29(2)–(3)), and full switching charges are banned from 12 January 2027 (Article 29(1)).

No, it cannot be registered. Under Article 18(c), an entity must operate on a not-for-profit basis and be legally independent from any entity that operates on a for-profit basis; a foundation legally controlled by a for-profit pharmaceutical group fails this requirement. Other Article 18 requirements (carrying out data altruism activities, legal person status, functional separation, and compliance with the Article 22(1) rulebook) would also have to be met.

For a qualifying entity, Article 19(5) provides that once all necessary information under paragraph 4 has been submitted and the competent authority has evaluated the application and found the entity complies with Article 18, it must register the entity within 12 weeks after receipt of the application. The registration is valid in all Member States, and the competent authority must notify the Commission, which includes the registration in the public Union register.

Data Governance Act - definition of 'data holder': a legal person, including public sector bodies and international organisations, or a natural person who is not a data subject with respect to the specific data in question, which, in accordance with applicable Union or national law, has the right to grant access to or to share certain personal data or non-personal data.

Data Act - definition of 'data holder': a natural or legal person that has the right or obligation, in accordance with this Regulation, applicable Union law or national legislation adopted in accordance with Union law, to use and make available data, including, where contractually agreed, product data or related service data which it has retrieved or generated during the provision of a related service.

Under the Data Governance Act a natural person can be a data holder only if they are not a data subject with respect to the specific data in question, whereas under the Data Act a natural person can be a data holder without that restriction. As to basis, the Data Governance Act status rests on having the right to grant access to or to share data, while the Data Act status rests on having the right or obligation to use and make available data, including product data or related service data retrieved or generated during the provision of a related service.
